Undetermined: the record can't determine this from what your group holds, and the reason is always given. An answer, not an error.
Withheld
Withheld: something is here that you can't see, kept back by its source or by who may see it. That it exists is shown, never hidden.
Unrated

Nobody looked: no one has searched for this yet. Not the same as “looked for, not found”.
Refused
Refused: Civicsmith won't do this. The reason says why, and what you can do instead.
Machine work

Not yet evaluated

Accepted by our group

Flagged

Found by search
Found by search: Civicsmith matched these words in what your group holds. Nothing is recorded: a member records it, from its passage, with the usual act.
To do

Noticed

Status

Working: not public; seen by your group's members.
Shared for review: named outsiders can read this draft until the owner stops sharing it.
Published: signed and public. It can be corrected by a new edition, never removed.

Hunch: a member's suspicion, labelled as one. Never evidence, and it never moves a finding.
Outward: this leaves your group's Civicsmith. Someone outside will see it.

Request records
Ask an office for records under the law that requires it to answer. The due date is worked out for you.
Action
One action your group took: what was sent, to whom, when a reply is due, and what came back.
Matter
A matter: what the group is pursuing about one problem, from the first letter to the outcome.
Case
Prepare a case for publishing: its scope, statement, findings, the people it names and why, its timeline and what it leaves out.
Review copy
A draft case shared with named outside readers before publishing. Their comments come back here.
Publication ceremony
The publication ceremony: the last checks, then signing. Publishing is permanent; corrections come as a new edition.
Published case
A case your group published, as anyone reads it: findings, their strength, the evidence, and how to check it without the group.
Another group's case
Another group's published case, recreated here. Nothing in it counts for your group until a member accepts it with a reason.
Docket
The public record of every edition, correction and withdrawal of your group's cases.
Inbox
Material handed to your group through its doorbell. Move it into the record, or discard it with a reason.
Hand material to the group
Hand material to the group. You need no account; the page says what will happen to what you send.

Installs Civicsmith in your group's own Cloudflare account under this short name. The short name is permanent: it appears in every address and beside every signature.
Runs Civicsmith's own checks on what was just installed, so you know it works before anyone joins.
Makes you the group's first administrator, using the one-time password from installing. Until it is claimed, nobody can use the group's Civicsmith.
Sets the name members and readers see. It can be changed later; the short name cannot.
Proves your group controls this web address, so published cases can show it as yours.
Chooses the places whose rules apply (deadlines, records laws, holidays) and the group's languages. Deadlines and wizards draw on these.
Lists the public offices and seats for your places, so requests and people can be addressed by role.
Adds something the record does not hold yet, such as an office, an organisation or a court case, with a note on where it comes from.
Names a place Civicsmith does not yet hold rules for. Administrators are told when an update brings it.

Keeps the group's material away from AI, for every use or the ones you choose. It binds every account, the group's, any project's and members' own. Members see your reason on Settings › The assistant.
Holds one Anthropic API key for the group, sealed and never shown again. It pays for a member's act when neither a project's account nor the member's own serves it.
Turns the group's key on or off without removing it. Members who rely on it are told what changed.
Chooses whether members are told, when they join and the first time they record something not public, what a court order could reach.
Records who holds the Cloudflare account. Whoever holds it can reach everything, so the group should know who that is.
Adds a security tool your organisation uses. Before it is turned on you see what it is sent, who receives it and how long it keeps files.
Creates an invitation for one person, under the cover the group knows them by. Nothing about them is public.
Saves what your group is, what it focuses on and why, and who may see each part: members only, or also the public.
Asks the assistant for a draft of your group's description, labelled as its draft. Nothing is saved until you keep it.
Shows who invited you, to which group, and what joining means, before you decide.
Sets the language Civicsmith speaks to you. Documents stay in their own language.
Joins the group with a handle and password. Your handle is how members see you; it need not be your name.
Starts from where you are: a problem you live with, a document, a deadline, a claim to check or a person. Each opens the right first step.
Changes what a member may do: contribute, administer. The change is recorded with who made it.
Changes a member's status, for example to inactive. Their past work stays in the record under their handle.
Adds your endorsement to make a member an administrator. With one administrator the group depends on one person.
Removes an administrator's powers, with a reason. It cannot leave the group with none.
Confirms a member's declared expertise, so it can be asked for when a check needs it.
Cancels an invitation nobody has used yet. The link stops working at once.
Creates a key that lets your group's website invite people, through an open form or an application someone approves.
Turns on one reusable link anyone with it can use to ask to join. You can turn it off at any time.
Removes the group's key for good. Members without their own account use Civicsmith without the assistant.
Shows how hard your group's Civicsmith was tried over the period you choose, against its usual. Counts only.
Sends a harmless test file or address to the tool and shows its answer, so you know it works before relying on it.
Stops using this tool. Notes it already wrote stay on the files they concern.
Says what you know professionally, such as accounting or law. An administrator confirms it; members can then ask you for checks.
Changes your password. Every other session signed in as you ends, so anyone using an old one must sign in again with the new password.
Registers the key you sign published cases with. Readers check a signature against it.
Withdraws your signing key, for example if it was lost. Cases already signed keep a record that it was withdrawn.
Chooses how quickly explanations open: promptly, or guidance on a longer pause so less opens while you move. Nothing is ever hidden.
Confirms you have read that your questions go to Anthropic under the group's account. Asked once, before your first question.
Confirms you have read what connecting your own account means: your questions go to Anthropic under your own account and terms.
Opens Anthropic's own sign-in page in a new tab, then connects your subscription with the code it gives you. Civicsmith never sees your password, and the code is used once and never kept.
Disconnects your Claude subscription from your group's Civicsmith. The group's key serves you instead, if the group has one.
Connects your own Claude API key. It serves only you, before the group's key, and Anthropic bills you for each use.
Disconnects your own API key and removes it from your group's Civicsmith. The group's key serves you instead, if the group has one.
Lists a tie that could matter to a case: an employer, a relative in a public body, a business interest. A case that concerns it says so.
Removes a tie from your list. A case already published keeps what it said.
Writes a note only you can see. Use it for thoughts not ready for the group.
Turns your note into something the group shares: an observation, a hunch or a question. The note itself stays private.
Changes your note. Notes are yours alone, so nothing else changes.
Deletes your note. If you turned it into something shared, that stays.
Asks the assistant to help word what you are writing, from what you typed. Its words arrive labelled as its draft; nothing is saved until you keep them.
Asks the assistant to draft translations of Civicsmith's words, labelled as drafts for a speaker to check.
Keeps a translation so members reading that language see it. Protected words need a second speaker's check first.
Lets a named member translate Civicsmith's words into one language.
Confirms a protected word as a second speaker, so members see it instead of the English.
Undoes a translation change in one step, back to what it replaced.
Shows the wizards your group can use: Civicsmith's, and those your group wrote.
Records a new wizard by walking through the steps yourself. It stays a draft until approved.
Changes a draft wizard's steps or words before it is submitted.
Submits a draft wizard for an administrator to approve before members are offered it.
Approves a wizard so members are offered it where its steps start.
Stops offering a wizard. Anyone part-way through can finish.
Does what this item asks, on the screen it concerns. It leaves your queue when done.
Passes this item to another member better placed to act, with a note.
Dismisses a suggestion or hint with a reason, kept on the record so the same thing is not raised again without cause.
Hides the item until the date you choose, when it comes back.
Stops this kind of item reaching you. You can turn it back on in your settings.
Moves your citations to the newer version of this document. You see what changed first.
Keeps citing the version you cited. The newer one stays in the record beside it.
Answers a reminder you set, for example that a reply came or a deadline passed.
Opens a question the group will answer with the record, from this hint, chain or suggestion. The source is kept with it.
Searches everything your group holds that you may see: documents, passages, questions, people.
Holds the items you picked together so one act can apply to them all. The set is held until the time shown.
Looks inside these documents for people, money figures, dates, requirements or a word. Each result shows its passage; nothing is recorded until you record it.
Lets the held set go. Nothing in it changes.
Shows where nobody has looked yet for this, so the group knows what an answer does not cover.
Has your group's Civicsmith fetch this address itself and keep exactly what the site sent, with when and from where.
Adds this file or photo to the record, with who made or obtained it and how. It waits in Held captures until vouched for.
Records what you saw or heard yourself as testimony: grade D, labelled as yours, never changed afterwards.
Asks for this to be captured later, for example when a site is down. The request waits until it can be fetched.
Watches this address and tells you when what it publishes changes. Each new version is kept beside the old.
Shows captures waiting for a member to vouch for them before they count.
Vouches that each copy is what its source gave, unaltered. It is signed with your name; it can be corrected later, never silently undone.
Sets the picked captures aside with one reason, shown to anyone waiting on them. They can be restored.
Brings a set-aside capture back, with a reason, so it can be vouched for.
Explains this copy's grade: how it was obtained and what would raise it.
Lists the archive's files by state: filed, already held, or not filed and why.
Opens the original file on your device. A low-risk file is checked first if its last check is over a week old.
Opens a high-risk original on your own device without a deeper check, after you confirm you will not enable macros or editing.
Shows a safe copy: each page as a picture, or a spreadsheet's figures as data. Nothing in it can run. Cite the original, not this.
Runs every check on this file: read whole, the built-in scanner again, and your group's outside tools. A clean result opens the original to everyone for 24 hours.
Gives your reason to release a file a scanner flagged. A second member's reason releases it; the machine never can.
Cites this passage in a question, as support or as cutting against it. A citation always points at the original document.
Stops using this copy in new work, with a reason. Questions that cite it are told.
Signs that this copy matches its source, adding your word to the capture. Signed with your key.

Says this name refers to a person the record already follows, with how sure you are (a grade) and why. It is shown as a claim, "claimed the same person, grade B, because…"; the records are linked, never merged, and anyone can see the reason or withdraw it with theirs.
Keeps asking this as new documents arrive; new matches reach your queue once, as a list.
Records a fact about this person from the passage: a position, a credential, an interest. It cites the passage.
Records a dated fact from the passage, citing it, for the timeline.
Works out a due date from the law and the dates, showing each day counted and each holiday skipped. It proposes the date; a member confirms it.

Switches one use on or off for this account: asking, drafting, runs, standing questions, suggestions, or exploring (No, Ask every day, Yes). An act this account would pay for, with its use off, stops; it never moves to another account.
Sets or removes one limit on this account: overall, for one use, or for each member's use, in dollars (estimated, API keys only), tokens or calls, a day or a month. It binds this account only.
Holds an Anthropic API key for this project, sealed and never shown again. Switched on, it pays for members' acts in the project, before their own accounts or the group's key.
Makes your own Claude sign-in the project's account, allowed only while you are its only member. If another member joins, it stops serving the project at once and you are told.
Turns the project's account on or off without removing it. While it is off, members' own accounts, then the group's key, serve in the project.
Removes the project's account. Members' own accounts, then the group's key, serve in the project from then on.
Records that you have read what the project's key means, before the first act it pays for.
Keeps this project's material away from AI, for every use or the ones you choose, with a reason every member sees. It binds every account, whoever pays.

Makes this project a counsel matter, your own project, or neither, with your reason. A counsel matter's correspondence and dates are seen only by its members and never published; your own project is hidden and yours alone.
Chooses which acts in this project need a second member's approval before they are sent: a kind of action, a tier, or anything addressed to the public. Your reason is kept with the setting.
Drafts a rule of your group's own, a deadline or a legal fact, from the captured document that states it. It applies only after another member confirms it.
Confirms a rule another member drafted, after checking it against its source. For a Tier 2 or Tier 3 matter you state your professional qualification.
Withdraws one of your group's own rules, with your reason. It is kept, and no longer applied.
Gives you the rule, its source and its confirmation as one exact file, to send to whoever keeps your places' shared rules.
Proposes an obligation from the body's own reply or report: a promise it made, or a response the report requires, quoting it. A member adopts it before it is tracked.
Lists the obligations adopted from these documents, and whether each is met.
Shows the routes your places' rules and your group give for this kind of action, each with the law or rule it cites. Legal information, not legal advice.
Changes when your standing question stops being asked again.
Records, in your group's own words, what it stands to gain or lose. It is shown beside your group's name wherever its work is published.
Lists the dates proposed for this action's clock that no member has adopted yet: each with its rule, its basis and who or what proposed it. Adopting one is a separate act.
Shows administrators how the website key and the join link are set, and every change to them, with who made it and when. Never the key or the link itself.
Asks the assistant to point out sentences that read as a claim of breach, a policy position, an ask for your group, or naming staff. It never rewrites them; you decide.
Asks the assistant to draft a documentation of what happened from the record, labelled as its draft until you make it yours.
Asks the assistant to propose how the reply bears on each claim, labelled as its proposal until you lay it out yourself.
Runs every publication check on this case and holds it, checked and unsigned, until it is signed. Nothing is published.
Shows whether this case's check still holds, and if not, why.
Checks your own text, sentence by sentence, against the record: supported, not supported, or contradicted. Only in your own project, and only you see it.
Links a later act of the same office, found compliant, as what corrected an act found noncompliant. Undoing the link needs a reason.
Records a success in your own words: what changed and when, what shows it, figures computed from the record, and the order of events or a cause you can show.
Puts an outcome (a success, a correction by the office, or a harm addressed) into the case's next edition. It is published when that edition is signed.
Records that what you sent was received by them, or served on them, how and when. A deadline may count from it.
Makes this action confidential, or not, with your reason. A confidential action is seen inside the group and never published; the change applies to what is published from now on.
Records a promise your group made to a person, such as an embargo or anonymity, or ends one.
Lists your group's other open actions with the same office. It is information, never a block.
Lays out the reply claim by claim: for each, whether it brings new evidence, disputes without evidence, or doesn't address it.
Proposes a claim-by-claim layout of the reply, labelled as a proposal and kept apart until a member lays it out.
Records that a project or a matter in a plan arose from this reply.
Records pressure that arrived outside any action, such as a letter, post or call. A legal threat can carry a litigation hold.
Records that you sent the litigation hold notice, with a copy or your account of how.
Records that a partner organisation approved the same text in its own copy. Their copy must match word for word.
Gives the second approval this project requires before sending. Only a member other than the first approver can give it.
Stops pursuing this escalation, with your reason. It is never recorded as ended or as a success, and it can be reopened where it stopped.

Asks the assistant for a first draft of this status report from the plan's items. The draft is labelled machine work, each line cites what it rests on, and nothing is saved until you save it as yours.
Starts a run on your own Claude sign-in, for you alone: checking this, or planning how to look into it. What it produces is labelled machine work and changes nothing until a member acts on it.
Reopens an escalation your group stopped pursuing, at the stage where it stopped, with your reason.
Sets this scenario aside, with your reason. It is kept whole, and can be restored.
Brings a set-aside scenario back, with your reason.
Pauses this plan, with your reason and, if you like, a day to look at it again. What it set running carries on.
Resumes a paused plan, with your reason.
Records, in your group's own words, the outcome it wants for this matter.
Takes this item's to-dos for yourself. Nobody assigns anybody; you choose.
Records that this plan set this watch running, so the plan knows to ask whether to keep it when it closes.
Keeps this watch until a date you choose, or stops it now.
Sets or removes the date to stop following this.

Has the assistant read up to 8 pages of this document that Civicsmith's own reading couldn't make out. The account that pays for your acts here pays, within its limits. Its words arrive labelled as the assistant's reading and stay undetermined until a member checks a passage against the page; the page images stay as they are.
Types the words of a page yourself, from its image. Your typing is labelled as yours, and a second member can check it against the page.
Lets the assistant explore today, on this account, what it said is worth exploring. Without a yes today, it doesn't.

Changes the handle the record shows on your work. Members see your earlier handle beside it, and no one else can ever take it. Allowed until your work first appears in a published case; after that it is fixed.
Checks, as you type, whether this handle can be used in the group: free, already taken, or using characters a handle can't have. It never says who has a handle.
Withdraws a mark on a photo, with your reason, for example when it covers what the finding shows. The withdrawal is recorded beside the mark; the public copy follows the marks that stand.
Marks anyone in a photo who is not part of a finding, and any number plate, so the copy a published case carries shows them obscured, labelled. The original stays inside the group.
Holds this requirement as a standard the city set itself, so questions can test the city against it.
Reads this figure into a money fact, with its stage and period, citing where it came from.
Says what a table's columns are, so its figures can be counted through a calculation rather than one by one.
Sets how strong an answer must be in this project before the group relies on it.
Invites a member into this project, so they can see and work on it.
Joins this project to see and work on it.
Opens a plan: what the group could do about what it found, its options and what each would take.
Removes this citation from the question, with the reason kept. It can be reinstated.
Puts a removed citation back on the question.
Narrows the question to what the record can answer, with the reason. The wider question is kept.
Records the group's answer to the question, from what it rests on. It can be withdrawn later, with a reason.
Withdraws the question's answer, with a reason, for example after new evidence.
Keeps a hunch beside the question, labelled as yours. A hunch is never evidence and never moves an answer.
Asks a member with the right expertise to check this, for example an accountant for figures.
Asks in plain words. The assistant answers only from what your group holds and says where it looked.
Shows how this answer was counted: the rule it applies, the rows it counted and the method, so you can check it rather than rely on it.
Stops asking this question on a schedule.
Asks the assistant to work on what this screen shows. Its results are labelled as machine work and become the group's only when a member accepts them.
Asks the assistant for suggestions here. Each is labelled as its suggestion, for you to adopt or ignore.
Stops the assistant's run. What it produced so far stays labelled as its draft.
Opens this person's page: positions, career and interests, each dated and cited.
Withdraws a claim that two records are the same person, with a reason.
Follows a public register (licences, filings) and tells you when an entry for this changes.
Removes a recorded value for good where the law or a court requires it. It cannot be undone by anyone; a marker stays where it was.
Records an event on the timeline from a cited source or your own testimony.
Adds who took part in an event, by name or by role.
Links two events, for example one caused or answered another, citing why.
Starts a money trail: the figures and transfers that follow one sum through the city's funds.
Includes this figure in the trail, with the reason.
Leaves this figure out of the trail, with the reason, so others see why.
Compares two sources' figures for the same thing and shows where they differ.
Compares what was committed with what was paid, period by period.
Shows what authorised this money: the vote, contract or rule, each cited.
Works out a figure from the record, with its method shown so anyone can repeat it.
Draws a random sample to check by hand, recorded so the draw can be repeated.
Binds your spreadsheet to the record, so its inputs come from cited documents and it can be recomputed.
Ties one of the spreadsheet's inputs to a cited place in the record.
Records that a second member checked the calculation, with what they found.
Accepts the result as a computed fact the group can cite.
Looks for chains of links between two people or organisations, each step cited and graded.
Uses a ready-made search, such as "money from a vendor to an official".
Checks each step of a chain against its sources and grades it.
Attaches a source to a step someone declared, so the step rests on evidence.
Adds a party to the proceeding by its role, citing where it appears.
Holds an order's requirements as obligations, so the group can check whether they are met and by when.
Links a decision to the law or order it interprets, citing the passage.
Confirms the due date, so reminders and the queue use it.
Reminds you on a date you choose. Only you see it.
Adopts a proposed standard as one the group holds the city to.
Relates the standard to the law it comes from, citing the passage.
Adds a subject to the plan: someone or something the group wants to act on.

Asks the assistant for options. They wait in the tray, labelled, until a member adopts one.
Adopts a suggested option into the plan as the group's own.
Chooses an option or declines it, with the reason kept on the plan.
Lays out what might happen if an option is taken, step by step.
Records how a checkpoint turned out, so the plan reflects what happened.
Shows what starting this option would do and anything that would stop it, before you start.
Closes the plan, with how it ended. It stays readable.
Starts the action: the group begins doing this option, from here to the send.
Prepares the text that will be sent, from the group's template or a labelled draft.
Prepares the filing with what the venue requires.
Approves this exact text for sending. Changing it afterwards needs approving again.
Records that you sent it, when and how. Civicsmith never sends for you; reply deadlines count from here.
Chooses the office it goes to, by role, so it reaches whoever holds the post that day.
Starts the records request as an action the group follows to its reply.
Chooses the records law the request goes under. It decides the deadline.
Moves the action to its next stage, with what happened.
Records a reply or letter received, with its date, so deadlines and the timeline follow.

Figure
What the amount is, in the words of its source: a transfer, a charge, a payment, a grant.
From
Who or which fund paid, as the source writes it. The payer is part of the figure itself, never guessed from somewhere else.
To, where it went
Who or which fund received the money, as the source writes it. "Not stated in this source" means this source does not say; record it from another source that does, citing the passage.
When it moved

The day the money actually moved, taken from the event the figure is tied to and the passage that dates it. A budget figure did not move, so it shows when it was adopted instead. Undetermined means no source the group holds gives the day; it is never guessed from the accounting period.
Stage

How far along the money was when the source counted it: adopted (budgeted), committed (promised by contract), or actual (spent; "paid" when the source shows the payment). Figures at different stages are compared, never added.
Period
The accounting period the source counts the amount in, such as a fiscal year, which need not match the calendar year. It is not the date the money moved: that is in When it moved.
Amount
The amount exactly as the source states it. A rounded amount ("about $2 million") keeps its rounding.
Source
The document the figure was read from, with its capture grade: how sure the group is that the copy is what the office published. Click the mark for the document.
In this trail?
Whether this figure counts in the trail's comparison, and the member's reason for including it or leaving it out. A figure left out stays listed, with why.
Kind
The kind of attempt that was turned away. Each counts attempts, not people.
This period
How many of this kind in the period you are looking at.
Usual
Your group's own median for the same length of time over the four weeks before. Far above it is what makes a period Raised or High.
Busiest hour
The hour with the most of this kind, and its count.
English

The words as Civicsmith ships them. Protected marks words that carry a ruling and need a second member's check before a translation is used; Local name marks a name kept as it is, with its explanation translated.
Español
The translation members see. A shaded cell is a draft, not yet shown to anyone.
Where it came from
Whether the translation came with a Civicsmith release, was typed by a member, or started as the assistant's draft, and whether it still needs its second check.
